info.title: HR-Avatar
info.description: HTTP API of the HR-Avatar avatar conversation engine: create, drive and tear down real-time avatar conversations.

get.description: The account's keys, newest first. Neither the key nor its hash is ever returned after creation.

next_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the next set of items.

post.description:
The response carries the full `key` once; it cannot be retrieved afterwards. A secret key
needs an explicit scope list, a publishable key needs 1 to 20 allowed origins. A key can only
issue keys of its own mode and, unless it holds `*`, only scopes it holds itself.

403.description: The caller lacks a requested scope (`insufficient_scope`) or asked for the other mode (`forbidden`).

post.description:
Takes effect at once. Revoking a key that is already revoked changes nothing and keeps the
original `revoked_at`. Revoking only removes access, so unlike create and rotate it needs
no scope or mode comparison with the caller: any key with `api_keys:manage` may revoke any
key of the account, itself included. The way back from a lockout is the `hra:issue-key` command.

Issues a successor with the same type, mode, scopes and origins, returned once as `key`. The
successor does not inherit an expiry: it has none until one is set by creating a key instead.
The old key keeps working for `overlap_seconds` (default 3600, 0 revokes it immediately) and never
outlives an expiry it already had. A revoked or expired key cannot be rotated.

403.description: The key carries a scope the caller lacks (`insufficient_scope`) or is of the other mode (`forbidden`).

409.description: The key is revoked or expired (`invalid_state`).

get.description:
The account's configs, newest first. `external_ref` keeps only those carrying exactly that
reference (case-sensitive, no wildcards); it is applied before the page is cut, so a host that
shares one account across its own customers never loses a config to the page size.

next_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the next set of items.

post.description:
`config` is checked against the settings the provider's adapter declares (`GET /v1/catalogue`):
an unknown key, a missing required key or a wrong value is a 422 naming `config.<key>`.
`llm_model_id` must be an enabled catalogue model; `voice` is `{engine, voice_id}` and the
engine must be one the provider speaks with. A config whose provider needs objects created for
it starts `pending`, any other `not_required`.

get.description: One config of the account. A config of another account, or a deleted one, is a 404.

patch.description:
Each member sent replaces the stored one as a whole; members left out are kept. The provider
cannot change. Changing the `config`, `persona`, `llm_model_id` or `voice` to something
different moves the config back to `pending` (or `not_required` when its provider needs
nothing for it); a change to the name or the reference leaves the sync state alone.

delete.description:
A soft delete: the config leaves the list and cannot start new conversations, and the
conversations that used it keep their reference to it. While a conversation that has not
finished (`created`, `connecting` or `live`) uses the config, it is refused with 409 `config_in_use`.

409.description: A conversation that has not finished uses the config (`config_in_use`).

post.description:
Queues a sync of the provider-side objects the config needs (for example a persona, a
language-model configuration or a bound voice) and answers 202 with the config, now `pending`.
Use it to retry a `failed` config or to push again a `synced` one. A config whose provider
needs no such objects is refused with 409 `invalid_state`.

409.description: The config needs no provider-side objects (`invalid_state`).

get.description:
For every provider: the settings its avatar configs accept (`fields` for `config`,
`persona_fields` for `persona`: key, type, whether required, limits and allowed values), the
resources it can list, and the voice engines it speaks with. The voice vendors that are not
avatar providers follow, each with the one resource `voice`. Makes no provider call.

Fetches what the account can pick from at the provider (for example avatars, voices, replicas
or personas) with the account's credential, else the platform's, and returns normalized
entries. `language` is set only when the provider states it. The result is cached for five
minutes per credential; `fresh=1` skips the cache. The provider's raw answer, errors and keys
are never returned.

422.description: No credential is available for the provider (`provider_credential_missing`).

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.

404.description: The provider does not list that resource.

502.description: The provider failed or could not be reached (`provider_error`).

post.description:
Returns a short audio sample of one voice as base64. The sentence is the platform's own for the
`language`; the request cannot supply text (any member beyond the four is a 422). A voice vendor
synthesizes that sentence; LiveAvatar returns its own generic clip. A provider that has no voices
of its own is previewed through the external vendor named in `tts_engine`; without one there is
nothing to preview (422). The vendor is called with the account's credential, else the platform's,
and a repeat is served from a cache without a vendor call. Every preview request counts against
a budget of its own per key (10 a minute by default, on top of the key's general budget), because
each synthesis is a paid vendor call; beyond it the answer is 429 with `Retry-After`.

422.description: The body is not valid, the voice has no vendor to preview it, or no credential is available for the vendor (`provider_credential_missing`).

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.

404.description: The vendor does not know the voice.

502.description: The vendor failed or could not be reached (`provider_error`).

post.description:
Starts the provider session for a conversation that has not been connected, and answers with what the
browser needs to join it. It can succeed once per conversation: a second call is `already_connected`.
The provider's and the language model's credentials are checked first; a missing one is a 422 that leaves
the conversation as it was. If the provider cannot start the session the conversation fails and the
answer is a 502 (a 429 when the provider is at capacity).

409.description: The conversation is already connected (`already_connected`), or is over (`invalid_state`).

422.description: The provider has no credential (`provider_credential_missing`) or the language model has none (`llm_credential_missing`).

429.description: The provider is at its concurrency limit (`provider_concurrency_limited`).

502.description: The provider could not start the session (`provider_error`).

post.description:
Stores a batch of 1 to 100 events (utterances and lifecycle signals) in order, once each: a
key sent before is counted in `duplicates` and not stored again, so a batch can be retried safely. One
invalid event rejects the whole batch (422). Events are taken while the conversation is open and for a
minute after it ended; later ones are `conversation_closed`. An utterance before the conversation is
connected is `invalid_state`. A `live` signal makes a connecting conversation live.

409.description: The conversation closed more than a minute ago (`conversation_closed`), or an utterance was sent before it was connected (`invalid_state`).

post.description:
Ends the conversation from the browser, with the reason `client`, and answers 200 with it. Ending a
conversation that is already over answers 200 with it unchanged.

Registers a conversation on one of the account's avatar configs and answers 201 with it, in
status `created`, plus a `client_secret` and its expiry. The secret is shown once: the host hands it
to the browser, which presents it with a publishable key to connect. Nothing is asked of the provider
or of any credential here; that happens when the browser connects. `external_ref` and `metadata` are
the host's own and come back exactly as sent. A config whose provider needs synchronizing must be
`synced` first (409 `config_not_synced`); a config of another account, or a deleted one, is a 404.

404.description: The avatar config does not exist, belongs to another account or was deleted (`not_found`).

409.description: The avatar config is still synchronizing, or its last synchronization failed (`config_not_synced`).

post.description:
Ends a conversation that is not over yet, with the reason `api`, and answers 200 with it. Its provider
session is released a few seconds later and its transcript is completed from the provider's. A
conversation that was never connected has no session: it ends at once and its transcript is final
(`ready`, empty). A conversation that is already over (ended or failed) is answered 200 as it is,
with nothing changed and nothing emitted, so ending twice is safe.

get.description:
One conversation of the account. Neither the client secret nor anything of the provider's (its
references, the callback token) is ever returned. A conversation of another account is a 404.

What was said in a conversation that has been connected, earliest first (by the time the browser or
the provider gave it, then by arrival; lines with no time come last). `status` is `pending` until the
provider's own transcript has been merged in, then `ready`, or `partial` when the provider's side could
not be had and only what the browser forwarded is here. A conversation that was never connected has no
transcript: 409 `invalid_state`.

One entry per credential provider. `source` says whose key a call would use: `account` (the
account stored one), `platform` (only the platform key is set) or `none`. `last_four` is
shown only for an account key of 12 characters or more.

put.description:
Creates or replaces the account's key for the provider. The key is encrypted at rest and is
never returned; the answer shows only its last four characters.

delete.description:
Idempotent: removing a key that is not stored answers 204 as well. Calls then use the
platform key, if one is set.

get.description:
The account's stored keys, shown as the provider and the last four characters of the key (null
for a key under 12 characters).

put.description:
Creates or replaces the account's key for a provider that appears in the model catalogue (404
otherwise). The key is encrypted at rest and never returned.

404.description: The provider does not appear in the model catalogue.

delete.description:
Idempotent: answers 204 whether or not a key was stored. A conversation whose config binds a
model of this provider then fails to connect with `llm_credential_missing`.

get.description:
The enabled entries of the platform catalogue. The catalogue is the same for every account
and cannot be changed through the API.
The account's endpoints, newest first. The secret is never returned after creation.

next_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the next set of items.

post.description:
The response carries the signing `secret` once (`hra_whsec_` and 64 hex characters); it cannot be
read afterwards. The URL must be https, at most 2048 characters, without credentials, and must not
point at a private or reserved address (plain http is accepted only in development environments).
An account holds at most 20 endpoints; the 21st is a 422.

get.description: One endpoint of the account, without its secret. An endpoint of another account is a 404.

patch.description:
Each member sent replaces the stored one; members left out are kept. A new URL is checked like the
URL of a new endpoint. The secret cannot be changed.

delete.description: Deliveries still waiting for a retry stop with it.

get.description:
Newest first, optionally only those in one `status`. Each entry says how many attempts were made,
the last response status, a short `last_error` code (`timeout`, `connection_failed`,
`destination_not_allowed`, `endpoint_disabled`, `internal_error` or `http_<status>`) and, for a delivery
waiting for a retry, when the next attempt is due. Neither the body that was sent nor anything a
receiver answered is ever returned. An endpoint of another account is a 404.
get.summary: List the deliveries of a webhook endpoint

next_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the next set of items.

get.description:
Always answers `{"status":"ok"}` while the process runs. It touches neither the database nor
Redis, so an orchestrator can use it to decide whether to restart the process.

Checks PostgreSQL and Redis. A failure answers 503 and names each dependency `ok` or `failed`,
never its address, version or connection string.

503.description: A dependency is unreachable; `checks` names each one `ok` or `failed`.

secretKey.description: Server-to-server secret key (`hra_sk_...`) sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.

clientSecret.description: Per-conversation `client_secret` JWT sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, always together with the publishable key.

publishableKey.description: Browser-safe publishable key (`hra_pk_...`); it grants nothing without the client secret.
publishableKey.name: X-HRA-Publishable-Key

ClientEventsRequest.description: A batch of the browser's events. The batch is validated whole: one invalid event rejects all of them.

events.description: One to a hundred events, applied in this order.

idempotency_key.description: The browser's own key for the event; sending it again is counted as a duplicate and stored once.

type.description: What happened: an `utterance` somebody spoke, or a `lifecycle` signal of the call.

occurred_at.description: When it happened, in ISO 8601 with a time zone.

role.description: Who spoke, for an utterance only.

text.description: What was said, 1 to 8000 characters, for an utterance only.

name.description: The signal, for a lifecycle event only: `live` (the call is up) or `error`.

data.description: Anything the browser wants to add, a JSON object of at most 2 KB.

ClientEventsRequest.title: ClientEventsRequest

ConversationStatus.description: Where a conversation is: `created -> connecting -> live -> ended | failed`. The transitions themselves are the lifecycle's business; this only names the states.
ConversationStatus.title: ConversationStatus

config.description: The provider-specific settings. The accepted keys depend on the provider: see `GET /v1/catalogue`.

persona.description: Provider-specific persona settings, or null for none.

voice.description: The voice to speak with, or null for the provider's default. `engine` must be one the provider speaks with.

CreateConversationRequest.description: The body of a conversation create. `external_ref` and `metadata` are the host's own and are carried untouched.

avatar_config_id.description: The avatar config to talk with: one of the account's, synchronized if its provider needs it.

system_prompt.description: The instructions the avatar follows. Kept as sent, whitespace included.

language.description: The two-letter ISO 639-1 code of the conversation's language, in lower case.

opening_text.description: What the avatar says first, if anything.

max_duration_seconds.description: How long the conversation may last, 30 seconds up to the platform ceiling. Defaults to 1800 (or the ceiling, if lower).

external_ref.description: The host's own reference, returned as sent and never interpreted.

metadata.description: The host's own JSON object, up to 8 KB encoded, returned exactly as sent and never interpreted.

CreateConversationRequest.title: CreateConversationRequest

url.description: Where the events are sent: an https URL of at most 2048 characters, without credentials and not on a private address.

events.description: The events to receive. All three when left out.

enabled.description: Whether events are sent to this endpoint.

description.description: A note of the host's own, up to 255 characters.

CredentialSource.description: Whose key a provider call would be made with, as the credential list reports it.
CredentialSource.title: CredentialSource

DeliveryStatus.description: Where a delivery is: `pending` until an attempt gets a 2xx (and while attempts remain), then `succeeded`, or `failed` once the last attempt has failed or the delivery was stopped.
DeliveryStatus.title: DeliveryStatus

EndedReason.description: Why a conversation reached a terminal state. The first writer wins and the value never changes.
EndedReason.title: EndedReason

EventType.description: The events an endpoint can subscribe to. The values are the `type` of the delivered body.
EventType.title: EventType

KeyMode.description: A label of the key space and its prefix. It never changes provider selection and never partitions data: both modes read and write the same account's resources.
KeyMode.title: KeyMode

PutCredentialRequest.description: The body of a credential write, shared by provider and language-model credentials.
PutCredentialRequest.title: PutCredentialRequest

SyncStatus.description: Whether an avatar config's provider-side objects match the config: `not_required` when the provider needs nothing created for it, `pending` after a change, `synced` once the objects exist and match, `failed` when the last attempt gave up.
SyncStatus.title: SyncStatus

TranscriptStatus.description: `pending` until the transcript has been reconciled with the provider's, then `ready`, or `partial` when the provider's side never became available.
TranscriptStatus.title: TranscriptStatus

UpdateAvatarConfigRequest.description:
A partial update: each member sent replaces the stored one as a whole (`config` is replaced, not
merged), each member left out is kept. The provider is fixed at creation; sending the one it
already has is allowed, any other is refused.

config.description: The provider-specific settings. The accepted keys depend on the provider: see `GET /v1/catalogue`.

persona.description: Provider-specific persona settings, or null for none.

voice.description: The voice to speak with, or null for the provider's default. `engine` must be one the provider speaks with.

UpdateAvatarConfigRequest.title: UpdateAvatarConfigRequest

url.description: Where the events are sent: an https URL of at most 2048 characters, without credentials and not on a private address.

events.description: The events to receive. All three when left out.

enabled.description: Whether events are sent to this endpoint.

description.description: A note of the host's own, up to 255 characters.

VoicePreviewRequest.description:
The body of a voice preview: which voice, and in which language to hear it. There is no member for the
sentence and no way to add one: any key outside these four is refused. The voice id is placed in a
vendor url, so it is limited to what an id is made of.

voice_id.description: The vendor's id of the voice: 1 to 128 letters, digits, `_` or `-`.

tts_engine.description:
The external engine the provider routes its voice through, or null. Needed to preview the voice of a provider
that has no voices of its own.

VoicePreviewRequest.title: VoicePreviewRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
